name: Abū al-Ṭayyib ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn ʿAlī al-Lughawī al-Ḥalabī
summary: Lexicographer of Aleppo whose Marātib al-naḥwiyyīn, 'the ranks of the grammarians', is one of the three oldest histories of the science; killed when the Byzantines took Aleppo.
bio: Abū al-Ṭayyib came from ʿAskar Mukram in Khuzistan, studied in Baghdad with Abū ʿUmar al-Zāhid, Thaʿlab's student, and settled in Aleppo at the court of the Ḥamdānids. His Marātib al-naḥwiyyīn sets out the grammarians and lexicographers of Basra and Kufa in order of rank and time, with judgements on their trustworthiness; with al-Sīrāfī's Akhbār and al-Zubaydī's Ṭabaqāt it is the oldest witness to how the grammarians saw their own past. His books on substituted letters (al-Ibdāl) and on words of opposite meanings also survive.
He was killed in 351/962, when the Byzantine army took Aleppo.
